original_prompt:
/oh-my-claudecode:autopilot In the Academy, GREK 101 and LATN 101 sessions are showing as locked after Session 1. 
All sessions except Session 1 show padlock icons and cannot be accessed.

Find where session locking is implemented in LanguageCoursePage.tsx (or wherever 
the lock logic lives for language courses) and change the unlock behavior so that:

1. All sessions are accessible by default — no prerequisite quiz score required 
   to progress between sessions.

2. The padlock icons should be removed from the session list sidebar entirely, 
   or replaced with accessible styling (no lock).

3. The is_admin check should also bypass any session locks (as a safety net), 
   consistent with the global admin bypass pattern.

Do not remove the quiz scoring functionality itself — students can still take 
quizzes and get scores. Just remove the hard gate that prevents accessing the 
next session without a passing score.

After the fix:
- All 10 sessions of GREK 101 should be accessible from the sidebar
- All 10 sessions of LATN 101 should be accessible from the sidebar
- Run tsc --noEmit to confirm clean
- This same pattern should apply to Sessions 11–20 once those are added

Do not touch PHIL course locking — only language course session locks.

On Arete Academy, courses show as unlocked on the dashboard and the session 
sidebar is navigable, but the actual session content page shows a locked/paywalled 
state when I click into a session. This affects PHIL 702, 703, 704, and the 
language courses.

The issue: the session content renderer (likely in [courseId]/[sessionId]/page.tsx 
or the SeminarPage/LanguageCoursePage component) has a separate tier check that 
gates content display. The admin bypass (is_admin column on profiles) was wired 
into course card visibility but not into the session content render path.

Fix:

1. Find every place in the codebase where session content is conditionally 
   rendered based on userTier, requiredTier, or subscription level.

2. Add is_admin check at each of those gates — if the user is_admin, render 
   the full content regardless of tier.

3. The is_admin value should already be available from the Supabase profile 
   fetch. If it is not being passed into the session content component, thread 
   it through from wherever the profile is loaded.

4. Do not remove the tier check for non-admin users — keep the paywall intact 
   for regular users. This is an admin-only bypass.

5. After the fix: log in as admin, navigate to a PHIL 702 session and a LATN 101 
   session, confirm full content renders without a paywall screen.

Run tsc --noEmit before and after. Report every file touched.
